overview.name: Scouts
overview.title: What is a scout?
overview.description: "A scout is a small agent (don't overthink that word) that looks at, wrangles, and makes sense of any data available in PostHog."
overview.notes: Opening line straight from Andy's post. Real examples: bundle size, CSP/web vitals, 404s, code complexity. ~30s

migration.name: Not just analytics
migration.title: Not just analytics
migration.imageAlt: Hedgehog salesman slapping the roof of a PostHog car covered in products: this bad boy can fit so many products in it
migration.description: Self-driving: "an autonomous loop that monitors your product for patterns and drafts fixes."
migration.notes: Before/after framing: instead of you going to the data, the data comes to you with a suggested action. Scouts are the watching piece – the next 4 minutes. The car joke tells itself. ~20s

skill-harness.name: Skill + harness
skill-harness.title: "A scout is, at its core, a skill"
skill-harness.description:
"The business logic that used to be a sprawl of if/else branches and helper functions now starts life as a few hundred lines of English anyone can read, write, and improve."

"What used to be if response_rate < 0.3 and sample_size > 30: is now a sentence like 'a flagship NPS survey needs ≥30 responses/week and a ≥10% score drop before it's worth acting on.'"

"Everything else – the loop, the sandbox, the scheduler, the memory – is deliberately thin plumbing around that skill."
skill-harness.notes: The tools are just the PostHog MCP – the same one Claude Code and Cursor use. Only three scout-only tools: emit signal, scratchpad, past runs. ~50s

scout-fleet.name: The fleet
scout-fleet.title: Scouts are skills: the real fleet
scout-fleet.imageAlt: Scout list in the PostHog Skills app
scout-fleet.description: "You start at the easy end and only reach for the heavier machinery when a particular scout actually needs it."
scout-fleet.notes: Point out the code-complexity scout created live at another meetup. ~20s

pipeline.name: Pipeline
pipeline.title: Scout → signal → report → action
pipeline.description:
• "A scout runs on a schedule, looks at some slice of your PostHog data, and decides whether anything is worth surfacing."
  • "If it is, the scout emits a signal – a semi-structured finding with evidence, and a suggested action."
  • "Signals get picked up by the self-driving pipeline, grouped, and turned into reports that land in your PostHog Inbox."
  • "Reports get actioned – by you, or automatically by a PostHog Code task that picks up the report and ships a fix or improvement."
pipeline.notes: The four steps, verbatim from the post. Restraint is the hard part – disqualifiers, dedupe keys, P0–P4 severity. ~35s

self-driving.name: Self-driving
self-driving.title: Signals → Inbox → Pull requests
self-driving.imageAlt: The self-driving section of posthog.com with Signals, Scouts, Inbox and Pull requests tabs
self-driving.notes: Screenshot of the public page. Scouts are one of four pieces: signals in, Inbox prioritizes, PRs out. ~15s

superpower.name: Superpowers
superpower.title: The superpower: an oracle + the tools to test against it
superpower.description:
Rewriting PostHog's SQL parser (posthog.com/blog/sql-parser):

  • "Having an oracle was critical ... finding some SQL that the parsers disagreed on, fixing the new parser to agree, and repeating."
  • "In shadow mode, I was able to test millions of parses quickly and there were zero divergences."
  • "On production queries, it was on average 454x faster than the previous parser."
  • "It was entirely written by Claude Opus 4.7, in Rust" – and still: "I wouldn't call this 'vibe-coded' at all."
superpower.notes: The secret is not the model – it is the validation loop: an oracle to compare against and tools (like MCP) to run the loop alone. Scouts are the same pattern applied to data. ~60s

web-analytics.name: Web analytics
web-analytics.title: The same pattern in web analytics
web-analytics.description:
• signals-scout-web-analytics: "acquisition channels diverging, attribution breakage, 404 spikes"
  • Our performance scout compares cache coverage, uncached p95, and failure rate against the fleet's own 7-day baseline
  • It caught a cache-coverage dip, filed a report in the Inbox – then updated the same report when the metric recovered
web-analytics.notes: The query-performance skill defines what "slow" means; the MCP provides the tools to measure. Next slide shows the real report. ~50s

scout-report.name: The report
scout-report.title: Caught the dip, tracked the recovery
scout-report.imageAlt: Web analytics performance scout report in Slack
scout-report.description: "The hard part of a scout isn't finding things. It's not finding things."
scout-report.notes: The update closes the loop – no new dashboard, nobody had to remember to check. The last reply in the thread gets the laugh and sets up the next slide. ~20s

reply-report.name: The conversation
reply-report.title: A report is a conversation
reply-report.imageAlt: Web vitals scout report in Slack with a human replying in the thread
reply-report.description: Reply in the thread, mention the agent, and ask for the next step.
reply-report.notes: In the print: the web vitals scout reports and I reply in the thread asking it to act. A report is not an email you archive – it is a conversation with whoever found the problem. ~25s

getting-started.name: Start today
getting-started.title: Start at the easy end
getting-started.description:
• Read: posthog.com/blog/what-is-a-scout · posthog.com/blog/sql-parser
  • Turn on: Self-driving / Inbox (open beta) – "PostHog ships with around 20 canonical scouts out of the box"
  • Run one anywhere: "you can run one manually in any agent surface where the PostHog MCP is available – PostHog Code, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, whatever."
getting-started.notes: Closing: a few sentences of English describing what is normal in your product – that is already a scout. ~30s

appendix-precompute.name: Appendix
appendix-precompute.title: Appendix: ask in Slack, the agent measures via MCP
appendix-precompute.imageAlt: Slack thread with the agent answering a precompute hit-ratio question with a chart
appendix-precompute.notes: Backup slide for Q&A: the same tools scouts use answer questions on demand.
